fact_sheet.business_description: SK hynix is a manufacturer of DRAM and NAND memory [D01]. The company is currently focused on an AI-memory mix and technology inflection, leveraging high-bandwidth memory (HBM3E) and DDR5 products to serve the AI accelerator ecosystem [D01, D03].
segments_and_separable_assets: Memory manufacturing (DRAM/NAND): Reported revenue of KRW 66.193 trillion for FY2024 [D02]. No segment-level EBITDA or separable asset valuation provided.
economics_vs_peers: Margins: SK hynix reported a 42% operating margin in Q1 2025 [D02, D03].
Peers: FY2024 operating margins were 5.19% for Micron, 10.88% for Samsung Electronics, and 1.79% for Western Digital [D06].
Capital intensity: The business requires large capital expenditures, with KRW 15.946 trillion in capex reported for FY2024 [D02].
capital_structure: Liquidity: KRW 14.3 trillion in cash and cash equivalents reported as of March 31, 2025 [D03].
Leverage: Debt/equity ratio of 29% and net debt/equity ratio of 11% as of March 31, 2025 [D03].
price_and_valuation: Rebased economic equity capitalization: KRW 201.2 trillion [D04].
event_or_catalyst_evidence: Catalyst: Earnings/product transition driven by HBM3E and DDR5 uptake in AI accelerators [D01, D07].
Outlook: Management expects FY2025 HBM demand to be approximately double 2024 levels [D03].
what_the_market_is_worried_about: Cyclicality/Competition: Risk that competitor qualification or AI spending corrections reverse margins while high capex commitments persist [D05, D06].
Execution: Yields, customer qualification delays, and export restrictions [D05].
Structure: Sensitivity to supply, pricing, and potential diminishing memory demand per workload in AI efficiency scenarios [D05].
recent_events: April 24, 2025: Q1 2025 financial results released, showing revenue of KRW 17.6391 trillion and operating profit of KRW 7.4405 trillion [D02, D03].
missing_data: Board composition, controller/government stakes, specific analyst consensus estimates, and current 13F/ownership data for the issuer.

As HBM demand doubles in 2025, the market will re-rate the stock to reflect its status as a critical, high-margin AI infrastructure play rather than a legacy memory participant [D03, D04, D07].

final.memo:
SK hynix is the preeminent beneficiary of the secular shift in AI computing architecture, yet the market continues to misprice it as a commodity memory cyclical, valuing the company at a depressed 5.89x EV/EBITDA [D03, D04]. While the broader industry remains tethered to volatile memory cycles, SK hynix has executed a pivot toward high-bandwidth memory (HBM3E) and DDR5 that is fundamentally changing its earnings profile [D01, D03, D07].

The math underpinning this inflection is stark. By annualizing the KRW 7.44 trillion operating profit delivered in Q1 2025, we project an annual run rate of KRW 29.76 trillion [D03]. Applying a 9.0x multiple—a modest premium for an AI infrastructure leader relative to its legacy peers—yields an implied equity value significantly higher than the current KRW 201.2 trillion capitalization [D04]. This stands in sharp contrast to the FY2024 operating margins of competitors such as Micron (5.19%) and Western Digital (1.79%), highlighting a margin gap that the market has yet to fully appreciate [D06].

Critics point to cyclicality and the risk of oversupply, but they miss the structural reality of the AI-memory bottleneck. Management has guided for HBM demand to double in 2025, a forecast we find credible given the ongoing capex cycle in AI accelerators [D03]. Our role here is to capture the re-rating that occurs as the company’s superior margins prove persistent rather than transient, signaling that the 'commodity' tag is obsolete [D03].

Downside is protected by a fortress balance sheet with KRW 14.3 trillion in cash and a conservative net debt/equity ratio of 11% [D03]. We are initiating a 4% position in the common stock, sized to reflect our conviction in the AI inflection [D03, D04]. We will hedge against sector-wide cyclical volatility through index puts and monitor the margin trajectory and yield stability closely, prepared to exit should the thesis break or competitive dynamics impair the company's margin advantage [D03, D05, D06].
